epics.notes: Completed by founder session 2026-08-07 (scaffolds verified; stale audit PRs closed).

epics.title: note_search empty-results investigation
epics.goal: Document why prod note_search can return empty while GET-by-id works; fix if a clear env/code bug.
epics.notes: REOPENED 2026-08-16: previous fix (PR #8, merged 2026-08-10) did not actually resolve the symptom — all 14 notes on personal-jacky were re-PUT 2026-08-11 to force re-embedding, and note_search still returned empty as of 2026-08-13, confirmed NOT a deploy-lag issue (running deployment postdates every relevant merge). Needs a fresh investigation: check whether MINIMAX_API_KEY is actually set in orbita-api's prod env on Zeabur, and whether note_put's embed call is failing silently again. If root cause needs new embedding provider spend or schema change, open decisions.json and mark needs_human. BLOCKS the hub: until search is trustworthy, agents must resume sessions via flat memory keys and note ids.

epics.title: Portfolio hub — multi-project reports + instruction dispatch
epics.goal: Orbita as Jacky’s central hub: ingest project reports, brief via chatbot, dispatch agent instructions into each repo for Cursor Autopilot.
epics.notes: Umbrella vision — stays proposed so Maker cannot invent hub direction. Sketch: docs/personal-steward/portfolio-hub.md. Decompose by approving concrete slices: E-08 (H2 retrieval), E-09 (collection), E-11 (on-demand trigger), E-12 (on-demand GitHub read) are approved slices. Remaining: instruction dispatch (H3, still proposed, needs github_dispatch credential — see D-002 _why_read_only).

epics.title: Notes list/filter for hub briefs
epics.goal: Agents can list notes by project, type, and date range without burning a reasoning loop or losing state across chat sessions.
epics.notes: First approved slice of E-07 (portfolio-hub.md H2). Additive read-only API; do NOT remove or change semantic /notes/search. Founder rationale 2026-08-07: chat sessions get rotated to avoid context overflow, so durable cross-project state must be queryable out of Orbita by a fresh session.

epics.title: Portfolio collectors — pull the three report lines into Orbita
epics.goal: Orbita collects autopilot, deployment and (later) runtime state for every registered project on a schedule, so one agent session can brief across the portfolio without crawling repos and dashboards by hand.
epics.notes: Founder + Claude session 2026-08-07. ARCHITECTURE (decided, do not relitigate): collection lives in ORBITA, not in each product. Rationale — (1) the autopilot line is already committed to git by Maker/Checker every run, so a product service would have to read its own repo to serve it, which is staler and inverts ownership; (2) the deploy line lives in Zeabur, one shared platform, so one credential covers all projects, whereas per-project reporting would put a Zeabur token inside each app; (3) only the runtime line genuinely requires the app, and no project has runtime signals worth reporting yet. Consequence: lines 1+2 cover all five projects with ZERO work in any product repo, and onboarding a new project is a registry row. CORRELATION KEY: git commit sha ties the lines together (task → PR → sha → deployment → serving version); without it we are correlating on timestamps, which is guesswork. Runtime line stays E-10 (proposed) until a product has real signals.

epics.title: Runtime report endpoints (per project)
epics.goal: Live products expose their own operational signals (signups, logins, queue depth) so the hub can see whether shipped work is actually being used.
epics.notes: The only line that genuinely needs per-project work — an app's own database is the only source. Deliberately NOT approved: no product has meaningful runtime signals yet (ai-business is pre-beta, ViOS is pre-UI). Building endpoints now buys a public surface and a credential per project in exchange for reporting zeroes. Approve per project when that project has users. Contract: ai-dev-methodologies portfolio-hub-reporting.md, edge=runtime.

epics.title: On-demand automation trigger — hub session can nudge a Cursor Automation early
epics.goal: From a hub chat session, Claude can trigger this repo's Maker or Checker to run now instead of waiting for its next scheduled tick — useful when interactively testing an idea or verifying a just-pushed fix — while keeping the exact same trust boundary the collector credentials already use.
epics.notes: Founder approved 2026-08-16, orbita ONLY as a pilot — do not generalise to other projects in this epic; that is a separate future epic once this one has been used for real. Manually decomposed by claude-hub-session 2026-08-17 (fast-tracked ahead of natural REPLAN, at founder's request — Maker's ready queue had T-0053 ahead of it, which would have delayed REPLAN by another cycle). MECHANISM (mirrors D-002 exactly, reuse packages/lane-credentials as-is, do not build a second vault): founder creates the Cursor Automation webhook URL + API key himself in the Cursor UI (Settings → this Automation → Webhook trigger, generated after the automation is saved) and stores them via the EXISTING POST /v1/admin/credentials route under client_id personal-jacky — Claude/Maker must NEVER see, enter, or transmit the raw webhook key; that step is founder-only, same as github_read and zeabur_api were. Credential names: cursor_webhook_orbita_maker and cursor_webhook_orbita_checker. T-0054 can build/typecheck/test fully before the founder has created either credential — end-to-end live verification happens once he does. HARD CONSTRAINTS (do not relitigate): orbita only; tool is read-only toward repo content (only ever POSTs to the stored webhook URL); no polling/retry/queueing — one call in, one webhook POST out; MCP-tool surface only, no new public HTTP route; an agent must never call trigger_automation on its own initiative — founder-requested every time, same trust level as sending a message or publishing content elsewhere in this hub's safety framework.

epics.title: On-demand GitHub read tools over MCP — hub session can query repo state from any device
epics.goal: From ANY hub session — including mobile, which has no first-party GitHub connector — Claude can read a file, list recent commits, or list pull requests for any registered project, using the credential the hub already has.
epics.notes: Founder approved 2026-08-17, motivated directly by a mobile session where GitHub's own connector was unavailable and status-checking had to wait for a desktop session. LOWER RISK THAN E-11: this is read-only toward GitHub with no path to mutating anything, so unlike E-11 there is no need to pilot on a single project first — it can cover every project the existing github_read token can already reach. REUSES THE EXISTING github_read CREDENTIAL FROM D-002 (2026-08-09) AS-IS — no new credential, no founder setup step required before this can work end-to-end. Manually decomposed by claude-hub-session 2026-08-17, same fast-track rationale as E-11. SCOPE (three tools, matching the actual read patterns used most often across this hub's sessions to date — do not add more without a real need): github_get_file(repo, path, ref?), github_list_commits(repo, branch?, limit?, since?), github_list_pull_requests(repo, state?). HARD CONSTRAINTS: strictly read-only — these tools must never call a mutating GitHub endpoint (no POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE to the GitHub API), matching the read-only rationale D-002 already gave for this exact credential; MCP-tool surface only, no new public HTTP route; never let the resolved token value reach a log line, error message, tool response, or committed file. NOT IN SCOPE for this epic (explicitly deferred): any write/mutating GitHub action — merging, commenting, creating branches or files — that remains chat-session-only via the first-party GitHub connector on desktop, this is intentionally NOT a path around that boundary; code search across a repo; any scheduling — these are called on-demand mid-conversation, not run on a timer.
